label: prf:em-spectral-completeness
title: Proof of em spectral completeness
html:
Proof. Proof of em spectral completeness

Proof. The braiding eigenvalue extraction (eigenvalue extraction) shows that c_{A,A} satisfies the Hecke minimal polynomial

  (c_{A,A} - q^{1/2})(c_{A,A} + q^{-1/2}) \;=\; 0

in E. The two eigenvalues q^{1/2}, -q^{-1/2} are distinct (their difference q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2} is a unit in R), so the minimal polynomial splits over R and Bezout produces orthogonal idempotents

  e_- \;=\; \frac{q^{1/2} \cdot \mathrm{id} - c_{A,A}}{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}},
  \qquad
  e_+ \;=\; \mathrm{id} - e_-.

These are central in E since c_{A,A} generates the centraliser of the diagonal R-action by Schur--Weyl-Hecke duality. Statement (2) follows from H_2(R, q) \cong E being free of rank 2 over R: E has at most two simple summands, and e_\pm realise them. The singlet identification V_- \cong \mathbf{1} is the standard Schur-functor decomposition A \otimes A = S^2 A \oplus \Lambda^2 A with \Lambda^2 A \cong \mathbf{1} when A is the fundamental of \mathrm{SU}_q(2). Statement (4) is the Wedderburn trace identity (Wedderburn trace) at n = 2. \square
